name: master.json
purpose: Self-improving project completion framework with principled design
philosophy: Think deeply. Build once. Evolve continuously. Principle-driven, not ceremony-driven.

dry.application: Single source of truth for patterns, skills, and configurations
dry.violations: Multiple definitions of same concept in different sections

solid.single_responsibility: Each component has one clear purpose
solid.open_closed: Extensible through skills/patterns, core principles immutable
solid.liskov_substitution: Skills must be interchangeable within same category
solid.interface_segregation: Clean boundaries between AI, skills, patterns, execution

pola.application: Behavior matches expectations, no surprising side effects
pola.validation: If it surprises a developer, it's a bug

yagni.application: Features added only when actually needed, not anticipated
yagni.enforcement: Every feature must solve existing problem, not theoretical one

composition_over_inheritance.application: Skills compose, don't inherit. Patterns combine, don't extend

principles: Fail safe to known good state
core.loop: discover → analyze → design → implement → validate → deliver → learn → improve

discover.goal: Understand context and identify applicable patterns

analyze.goal: Deep problem understanding with constraint mapping

implement.goal: Build solution executing skills and patterns

learn.goal: Extract lessons and harvest successful patterns
learn.output: Updated skill library and framework improvements

diagnostics.policy: logs must enable end-to-end reconstruction of decisions

decision_framework.bayesian_updates: Learn from outcomes to improve future decisions
decision_framework.confidence_tracking: Know when to escalate to human judgment
decision_framework.principle_validation: Check against design principles before acting

enforcement.interpreter_note: Continuous feedback loop for intelligent system behavior adaptation

safety_protocols.explainable: All AI decisions must have clear rationale

error_recovery.skill_failure_cascade: Detect and isolate failing skills to prevent spread
error_recovery.partial_failure_modes: Continue degraded operation when subset fails
error_recovery.root_cause_guidance: Suggest probable causes and next actions

context_management.project_switching: Persist mental state and next-actions per project
context_management.interrupted_workflow_recovery: Resume exactly where left off with run_id/trace_id

resource_intelligence.bottleneck_prediction: Predict and surface likely bottlenecks early

security_by_design.threat_modeling: Perform lightweight STRIDE-like checks per change

technical_debt.prioritization: Rank by impact and fix effort

hot_evolution.live_skill_updates: Safely update skills mid-run with rollback
hot_evolution.pattern_migration: Migrate to better patterns without downtime
hot_evolution.framework_versioning: A/B new framework behaviors behind flags

predictive_intelligence.failure_prediction: Identify likely failure points before they occur

dependency_intelligence.conflict_resolution: Auto-resolve version conflicts with safety checks

human_factors.energy_optimization: Schedule demanding tasks when energy is high

harvesting.skill_synthesis: Combine primitive skills into higher-order capabilities
harvesting.failure_analysis: Learn from errors to prevent recurrence

shell.structure: Set options, source shared, declare variables, implement functions
shell.variables: UPPER_CASE for constants, lower_case for locals

ruby.structure: Require dependencies, define modules/classes, implement logic

universal.idempotency: Operations safe to repeat without side effects
universal.observability: Always know system state and health
universal.reversibility: Every change can be undone safely
universal.composability: Small pieces combine into larger behaviors

rails.hotwire_progressive_enhancement: Start with server-rendered, enhance with JS
rails.api_first_design: Build API, then consume it in frontend

openbsd.privilege_separation: Each service runs with minimal required privileges
openbsd.native_tooling: Prefer base system tools over third-party dependencies
openbsd.security_by_default: Secure configuration is the default configuration

perspectives.security: Attack vectors, privilege boundaries, data protection

strategies.contract_testing: Validate API boundaries and service interactions
strategies.regression_testing: Ensure changes don't break existing functionality
strategies.performance_benchmarking: Measure impact of changes on system performance

metrics.developer_velocity: Time from idea to production deployment
metrics.system_reliability: Uptime and error rates in production
metrics.framework_effectiveness: Skills reused per project, patterns harvested

discovery.problem: What specific problem are we solving?
discovery.users: Who is affected and how will their experience change?
discovery.patterns: What applicable patterns exist in our skill library?

design.simplicity: What is the simplest approach that completely solves the problem?
design.composition: How do existing skills and patterns combine for this solution?
design.alternatives: What other approaches did we consider and why reject them?
design.principles: How does this design comply with our principles?

implementation.testing: How do we prove this works correctly?
implementation.monitoring: How will we know if this fails in production?
implementation.rollback: How do we undo this if something goes wrong?
implementation.maintenance: Who will maintain this and how?

learning.harvest: What patterns from this project can be reused?
learning.improvement: How can we make the framework better for next time?
learning.optimization: What inefficiencies did we discover and eliminate?

process.health_checks: Verify system health before and after deployment
process.gradual_rollout: Deploy to subset, validate, then complete rollout

learning.every_execution: Extract lessons from each project completion
learning.skill_optimization: Skills become more effective through usage
learning.principle_refinement: Design principles evolve based on experience

adaptation.safety_first: Never compromise core safety or reliability

anti_patterns.complexity: Adding unnecessary features or overengineering simple solutions
anti_patterns.fragility: Systems that break easily or require careful handling
anti_patterns.opacity: Code or behavior that's difficult to understand or debug
anti_patterns.rigidity: Systems resistant to change or extension
anti_patterns.operational_complexity: Deployment or maintenance processes that are overly complicated
anti_patterns.ceremony_over_substance: Process that exists to satisfy the process
anti_patterns.undocumented_magic: Behavior that surprises or confuses users

meta.type: Self-improving reasoning framework with principled design
meta.evolution: Framework learns continuously while maintaining design integrity
meta.compatibility: Any language, platform, or paradigm through adaptive composition
meta.philosophy: Maximum capability through principled simplicity, not clever complexity
